newsitem.title: USA: IBP Illinois cattle plant workers to strike.
newsitem.headline: IBP Illinois cattle plant workers to strike.

text.p: Workers at IBP Inc's cattle slaughter and processing plant in Joslin, Ill., voted to strike at 0100 CST on Tuesday, officials said.
"The union voted over the weekend to go on strike after rejecting our last, best and final offer," said IBP company spokesman Gary Mickelson.
The plant, located near Moline, has a daily slaughter capacity of 3,000 to 4,000 head, according to trade sources.
About 1,800 workers represented by the United Food and Commercial Workers Union (UFCW) Local 1540 will be affected by the strike, Mickelson said.
"The people voted Saturday almost unanimously to go on strike," Bob Hooker, secretary-treasurer of Local 1540, told Reuters.
Contract negotiations last week that involved a federal mediator failed to resolve differences between the plant's meatcutters and IBP, Hooker said.
The existing four-year contract expired on October 20.
IBP will shift production to other beef plants and continue to aggressively buy cattle in the Joslin area market, Mickelson added.
The rejected offer included an $0.80 per hour base pay increase over the next 36 months, which would include an immediate $0.40 increase, Mickelson said.
"These increases would move base production wages to more than $9 per hour and top production wages into the $10-$11 range," Mickelson said.

The offer also included an immediate signing bonus of $400 for employees hired on or before Nov 9, 1995, and a $100 bonus for employees hired after that date, he said. Maintenance worker wages would also have been increased.
Hooker said the union was agreeable to IBP's pay offer but objected to proposals to scale back insurance coverage and cancel a profit-sharing plan.
